top_signals.title: The Energy Transition Needs More Metals but Less Extraction
top_signals.summary: The energy transition is often described as a switch from one extraction industry to another. Instead of digging up coal and drilling for oil, the argument goes, we will simply dig up enormous quantities of lithium, copper and nickel. There is some truth in that description. More mines will be needed for several important metals. But it misses the much larger change taking place underneath. A renewable and electrified energy system can require substantially less ongoing extraction than the fossil system it replaces. The world can need more copper…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.
